> [!example] Scenario
> Create 2 Vlans from the main switch and let the other switch be configured too and let pc0 access one vlan and pc1 access the other vlan
> 
> VLAN 200 FACULTY
> VLAN 300 STUDENT

# How to start
## prepare 2 switches
1. ![[Pasted image 20261022080949.png]]
2. ![[Pasted image 20261022081039.png]]

## Prepare 2 pcs
![[Pasted image 20261022081135.png]]

## connect 2 switches on gigabit Ethernet
connect both using a cross over cable
![[Pasted image 20261022081259.png]]![[Pasted image 20261022081350.png]]

## connect both pcs to lower switch
connect pc0 and pc1 to lower switch using a straight through cable on any **fast ethernet** port
![[Pasted image 20261022081542.png]]

# the setup
before anything, remember the exit ritual you'll do over and over: `no shutdown` → `exit` → `do wr` — [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]

## enter the main switch (3560)
click the switch → **cli** tab, then — [[Cisco Commands#Enable Switch | enable guide]], [[Cisco Commands#access configuration commands | configure terminal guide]]
```cisco
Switch>                 enable
Switch#                 configure terminal
Switch(config)#
```

# main switch (3560)
## create vlan 200 first
create it and give it its name — [[Cisco Commands#create and configure vlan | create vlan guide]], [[Cisco Commands#rename vlan | rename vlan guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 200
Switch(config-vlan)#    name FACULTY
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

then give vlan 200 its svi (the gateway ip for that whole vlan) — [[Cisco Commands#enter vlan interface and setup vlan ip address | vlan interface + ip address guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface vlan 200
Switch(config-if)#      ip address 192.168.5.1 255.255.255.0
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## create vlan 300 after
same pair of commands as vlan 200 — [[Cisco Commands#create and configure vlan | create vlan guide]], [[Cisco Commands#rename vlan | rename vlan guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 300
Switch(config-vlan)#    name STUDENT
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

then the svi for vlan 300 — [[Cisco Commands#enter vlan interface and setup vlan ip address | vlan interface + ip address guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface vlan 300
Switch(config-if)#      ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

> [!tip] after the vlan 300 svi you'll see the link up messages like this
> `%LINK-5-CHANGED: Interface Vlan300, changed state to up`

## trunk on the main switch (3560)
enter the gigabit port that points at the 2950, then trunk it — [[Cisco Commands#enter ethernet port interface | enter interface guide]], [[Cisco Commands#configure switchport to be mode trunk | trunk guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
> [!warning] the `encapsulation dot1q` line is only needed/possible on the 3560
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface gigabitEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

after this the main switch side is done — it should show Vlan200 and Vlan300 up in `show ip interface brief`

# second switch (2950)
## enter the second switch
it's a different device, so you have to enable + configure terminal on it again:
```cisco
Switch>                 enable
Switch#                 configure terminal
Switch(config)#
```

> [!note] check the pc ports first
> hover the cable ends or run `show ip interface brief` to see which fast ethernet ports pc0/pc1 are actually plugged into — we use Fa0/1 and Fa0/2 below

## trunk on the second switch (2950)
the 2950 only supports 802.1Q so there is **no** `switchport trunk encapsulation` command here — just mode trunk. [[Cisco Commands#configure trunk on the second switch | second switch trunk guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface gigabitEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## create vlan 200 on the second switch
the 2950 needs its own copy of the vlans (vtp may sync them over the trunk, but making them by hand is safer) — [[Cisco Commands#create the vlans on the second switch | second switch vlan guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 200
Switch(config-vlan)#    name FACULTY
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## create vlan 300 on the second switch
same as vlan 200 above — [[Cisco Commands#create the vlans on the second switch | second switch vlan guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 300
Switch(config-vlan)#    name STUDENT
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## access ports — 2 things to assign
### pc0's port → vlan 200
enter the fast ethernet port pc0 is on, make it an access port and put it in vlan 200 — [[Cisco Commands#assign access ports to vlans | access port guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface fastEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#      switchport access vlan 200
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

### pc1's port → vlan 300
same access block, different port and vlan — [[Cisco Commands#assign access ports to vlans | access port guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface fastEthernet 0/2
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#      switchport access vlan 300
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

# the pcs
## set the ips — 2 things to configure
click the pc → **desktop** tab → **ip configuration** → static — [[Cisco Commands#setup pc ip addresses | pc ip setup guide]]

pc0 (vlan 200/FACULTY):
| field | value |
|-------|-------|
| ip address | 192.168.5.10 |
| subnet mask | 255.255.255.0 |
| default gateway | 192.168.5.1 |

pc1 (vlan 300/STUDENT):
| field | value |
|-------|-------|
| ip address | 192.168.10.10 |
| subnet mask | 255.255.255.0 |
| default gateway | 192.168.10.1 |

> [!tip] the gateway is the svi ip of that vlan on the main switch — that's what you configured earlier

# main switch again (optional but do it)
## enable ip routing
the 3560 doesn't route between svis by default, so without this pc0 can never ping pc1. go back to the 3560's cli (config mode) and turn routing on — [[Cisco Commands#enable ip routing (optional) | ip routing guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         ip routing
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

# verify
make sure you're at `Switch#` (privileged exec, not config mode) and run these on **both** switches — [[Cisco Commands#verify | verify guide]]
```cisco
Switch#                 show vlan brief
Switch#                 show interfaces trunk
Switch#                 show ip interface brief
```

then from a pc (desktop → command prompt):
```bash
ping 192.168.10.10
```
first ping may drop 1-2 packets (arp) — run it again, it should pass

Switch(config-if)#      exit

Switch(config)#         vlan 300
Switch(config-vlan)#    name ACCOUNTING
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit

Switch(config)#         interface vlan 300

> [!tip] after the vlan 300 svi you'll see the link up messages like this

## trunk on the main switch (3560)
this time **two** gigabit ports get trunked — `Gi0/1` points at switch0 and `Gi0/2` points at switch1, so run the same block twice — [[Cisco Commands#enter ethernet port interface | enter interface guide]], [[Cisco Commands#configure switchport to be mode trunk | trunk guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]

the 2950 only supports 802.1Q so there is **no** `switchport trunk encapsulation` command here — just mode trunk. [[Cisco Commands#configure trunk on the second switch | second switch trunk guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]

```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface fastEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#      switchport access vlan 200
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit

|--------|------|------------|-------------|-----------------|

```bash

```

# Cisco Commands
## Enable Switch
**prompt:** `Switch>`
```bash
enable
```

## access configuration commands
**prompt:** `Switch#`
```bash
configure terminal
```

## create and configure vlan
**prompt:** `Switch(config)#`
```bash
vlan [vlan number]
```
> [!tip] Example
> prompt changes to `Switch(config-vlan)#` after you type the vlan command
> ```cisco
> vlan 200
> ```

## rename vlan
**prompt:** `Switch(config-vlan)#`
```cisco
name [vlan name]
```
> [!tip] example
> ```cisco
> name FACULTY
> ```

## enter vlan interface and setup vlan ip address
enter vlan interface
**prompt:** `Switch(config)#`
```cisco
interface vlan [vlan number]
```
setup vlan ip address
**prompt:** `Switch(config-if)#`
```bash
ip address [ip address] [subnet mask]
```

> [!tip] example
> ```cisco
> Switch(config)#         interface vlan 200
> Switch(config-if)#      ip address 192.168.5.1 255.255.255.0
> ```

after this you do [[#setup for exit]](click me).

## enter ethernet port interface
**prompt:** `Switch(config)#`
```cisco
interface [port type] [port number]
```
> [!tip] example
> ```
> interface GigabitEthernet 0/1
> ```

## configure switchport to be mode trunk
**prompt:** `Switch(config-if)#`
```cisco
switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
```

```cisco
switchport mode trunk
```

> [!quote] result
> ```cisco
> Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode trunk
> 
> Switch(config-if)# 
> 
> %LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to down
> 
> %LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to up
> 
> %LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface Vlan200, changed state to up
> 
> %LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface Vlan300, changed state to up
> ```

after this, do [[#setup for exit]].

> [!warning] this trunk config is only for the main switch (3560)
> the lower switch (2950T-24) only supports 802.1Q, so `switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q` does not exist on it. on the 2950 just do `switchport mode trunk` (see [[#configure trunk on the second switch]]).

after that, the main switch will show up with these vlans
![[Pasted image 20261022090540.png]]


## setup for exit
do these series of steps when exiting
you start at `Switch(config-if)#` — after `exit` the prompt changes to `Switch(config)#`, that's normal
```cisco
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## configure trunk on the second switch
on the lower switch (2950T-24), enter the port connected to the main switch
**prompt:** `Switch(config)#`
```cisco
interface gigabitEthernet 0/1
```

> [!warning] no encapsulation command here
> the 2950 only supports 802.1Q so `switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q` does not exist on it. just do:
**prompt:** `Switch(config-if)#`
```cisco
switchport mode trunk
```

after this, do [[#setup for exit]].

## create the vlans on the second switch
the second switch needs the same vlans (create them manually, vtp may sync them over the trunk but doing it by hand is safer for the lab)
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 200
Switch(config-vlan)#    name FACULTY
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         vlan 300
Switch(config-vlan)#    name STUDENT
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
```

## assign access ports to vlans
this is what actually puts the pcs inside the vlans. enter the fast ethernet port each pc is connected to

> [!note] check your ports first
> hover over the cable ends on the topology or run `show ip interface brief` on the lower switch to see which fast ethernet port each pc is actually plugged into

pc0 port → vlan 200:
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface fastEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#      switchport access vlan 200
```

pc1 port → vlan 300:
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface fastEthernet 0/2
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#      switchport access vlan 300
```

after each one, do [[#setup for exit]].

## setup pc ip addresses
click the pc → **desktop** tab → **ip configuration** → set to static

| pc | ip address | subnet mask | default gateway |

# the setup
before anything, remember the exit ritual you'll do over and over: `no shutdown` → `exit` → `do wr` — [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]

## enter the main switch (3560)
click the switch → **cli** tab, then — [[Cisco Commands#Enable Switch | enable guide]], [[Cisco Commands#access configuration commands | configure terminal guide]]
```cisco
Switch>                 enable
Switch#                 configure terminal
Switch(config)#
```

# main switch (3560)
## create vlan 100 first
create it and give it its name — [[Cisco Commands#create and configure vlan | create vlan guide]], [[Cisco Commands#rename vlan | rename vlan guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 100
Switch(config-vlan)#    name STUDENT
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

then give vlan 100 its svi (the gateway ip for that whole vlan) — [[Cisco Commands#enter vlan interface and setup vlan ip address | vlan interface + ip address guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface vlan 100
Switch(config-if)#      ip address 192.168.2.1 255.255.255.0
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## create vlan 200 after
same pair of commands as vlan 100 — [[Cisco Commands#create and configure vlan | create vlan guide]], [[Cisco Commands#rename vlan | rename vlan guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 200
Switch(config-vlan)#    name FACULTY
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

then the svi for vlan 200 — [[Cisco Commands#enter vlan interface and setup vlan ip address | vlan interface + ip address guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface vlan 200
Switch(config-if)#      ip address 192.168.3.1 255.255.255.0
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

> [!tip] after the vlan 200 svi you'll see the link up messages like this
> `%LINK-5-CHANGED: Interface Vlan200, changed state to up`

## trunk on the main switch (3560)
enter the gigabit port that points at the 2960, then trunk it — [[Cisco Commands#enter ethernet port interface | enter interface guide]], [[Cisco Commands#configure switchport to be mode trunk | trunk guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
> [!warning] the `encapsulation dot1q` line is only needed/possible on the 3560
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface gigabitEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

after this the main switch switching side is done — it should show Vlan100 and Vlan200 up in `show ip interface brief`

# sub switch (2960)
## enter the sub switch
it's a different device, so you have to enable + configure terminal on it again:
```cisco
Switch>                 enable
Switch#                 configure terminal
Switch(config)#
```

> [!note] check the pc ports first
> hover the cable ends or run `show ip interface brief` to see which fast ethernet ports pc0/pc1 are actually plugged into — we use Fa0/1 and Fa0/2 below

## trunk on the sub switch
the 2960 only supports 802.1Q so there is **no** `switchport trunk encapsulation` command here — just mode trunk. [[Cisco Commands#configure trunk on the second switch | second switch trunk guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface gigabitEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## create the 2 vlans on the sub switch
the sub switch needs its own copy of the vlans (vtp may sync them over the trunk, but making them by hand is safer) — [[Cisco Commands#create the vlans on the second switch | second switch vlan guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 100
Switch(config-vlan)#    name STUDENT
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         vlan 200
Switch(config-vlan)#    name FACULTY
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## access ports — 2 things to assign
### pc0's port → vlan 100
enter the fast ethernet port pc0 is on, make it an access port and put it in vlan 100 — [[Cisco Commands#assign access ports to vlans | access port guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface fastEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#      switchport access vlan 100
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

### pc1's port → vlan 200
same access block, different port and vlan — [[Cisco Commands#assign access ports to vlans | access port guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface fastEthernet 0/2
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#      switchport access vlan 200
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

> [!warning] do NOT add svis on the sub switch — no `interface vlan 100` / `interface vlan 200` with ip addresses here
> the sub switch is layer 2 only — the 3560 is the **only** device allowed to own `192.168.2.1` / `192.168.3.1`. if both switches hold the same ip:
> - the dhcp server pings an address before leasing it and gets a reply from the sub switch → `%DHCPD-4-PING_CONFLICT: DHCP address conflict: server pinged 192.168.2.1`
> - pcs can't tell which switch answers when they look for the gateway → pings die
> 
> if it already happened, delete the svis on the sub switch (`no interface vlan` removes the ip interface — the vlans, ports and trunk keep working):
> ```cisco
> Switch(config)#         no interface vlan 100
> Switch(config)#         no interface vlan 200
> Switch(config)#         do wr
> ```

# DHCP pools (back on the main switch)
this is the part that makes it a dhcp lab — everything below happens on the **3560's** cli (config mode). click back to the main device first

## exclude the gateway addresses first
a pool leases the whole `/24` starting at `.1` unless told not to — and `.1` is the svi you just made. exclude it on both subnets
**prompt:** `Switch(config)#`
```cisco
Switch(config)#         ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.2.1
Switch(config)#         ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.3.1
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## create the vlan100 pool
**prompt:** `Switch(config)#`
```cisco
ip dhcp pool vlan100
```

the prompt changes to `Switch(dhcp-config)#` — a pool needs 3 things:
```cisco
Switch(dhcp-config)#    network 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0
Switch(dhcp-config)#    default-router 192.168.2.1
Switch(dhcp-config)#    dns-server 192.168.2.1
Switch(dhcp-config)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

> [!tip] what the 3 lines mean
> - `network` — the range being handed out: `192.168.2.0/24` (minus the excluded `.1`)
> - `default-router` — the gateway pushed to the pc = the vlan 100 svi
> - `dns-server` — here it matches the svi too

## create the vlan200 pool
same block, vlan 200 numbers (`default-router` = the vlan 200 svi):
```cisco
Switch(config)#         ip dhcp pool vlan200
Switch(dhcp-config)#    network 192.168.3.0 255.255.255.0
Switch(dhcp-config)#    default-router 192.168.3.1
Switch(dhcp-config)#    dns-server 192.168.3.1
Switch(dhcp-config)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## enable ip routing
same "optional but do it" step as the other labs — without it the pcs can never ping across vlans even with dhcp — [[Cisco Commands#enable ip routing (optional) | ip routing guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         ip routing
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

> [!tip] switched on the pools late, or already saw a `%DHCPD-4-PING_CONFLICT`?
> the server remembers old conflicted addresses. clear the lease table and let the pcs re-request — [[Cisco Commands#verify | verify guide]]
> ```cisco
> Switch#                 clear ip dhcp binding *
> ```

# the pcs
## get the ips via dhcp — 2 devices
click the pc → **desktop** tab → **ip configuration** → select **DHCP** (instead of typing a static set) — [[Cisco Commands#setup pc ip addresses | pc ip setup guide]]

no ip, mask, gateway or dns to type — the pool fills them all in (the pc shows "DHCP request successful"):
| pc | vlan | what it gets |
|----|------|--------------|
| pc0 | 100 STUDENT | `192.168.2.x` / `255.255.255.0` / gateway `192.168.2.1` |
| pc1 | 200 FACULTY | `192.168.3.x` / `255.255.255.0` / gateway `192.168.3.1` |

> [!tip] how to renew a lease
> the exact leased address depends on order, so check it: desktop → **command prompt** → `ipconfig`. if a pc is holding stale settings from an earlier attempt, toggle the radio to static then back to dhcp — that forces a fresh request. don't panic if pc0 keeps `192.168.2.2` and pc1 keeps `192.168.3.2` every time, dhcp reuses the next free address

# verify
on the switches, make sure you're at `Switch#` (privileged exec, not config mode) and run the standard trio on **both** — [[Cisco Commands#verify | verify guide]]
```cisco
Switch#                 show vlan brief
Switch#                 show interfaces trunk
Switch#                 show ip interface brief
```

on the 3560 you can also watch the leases:
```cisco
Switch#                 show ip dhcp binding
```

then from a pc (desktop → command prompt):
```bash
ipconfig
```
shows the leased ip/mask/gateway — pc0 should be `192.168.2.x` with gateway `192.168.2.1`

```bash
ping 192.168.3.2
```
inter-vlan test — pc0 (STUDENT) pinging pc1 (FACULTY) needs `ip routing` on the 3560. if `192.168.3.2` isn't pc1's actual address, ping whatever `ipconfig` showed on pc1

first ping may drop 1-2 packets (arp) — run it again, it should pass. ping `192.168.3.1` too if you want to hit the gateway directly

# the setup
before anything, remember the exit ritual you'll do over and over: `no shutdown` → `exit` → `do wr` — [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]

## enter the main switch (3560)
click the switch → **cli** tab, then — [[Cisco Commands#Enable Switch | enable guide]], [[Cisco Commands#access configuration commands | configure terminal guide]]
```cisco
Switch>                 enable
Switch#                 configure terminal
Switch(config)#
```

# main switch (3560)
## create vlan 100 first
create it and give it its name — [[Cisco Commands#create and configure vlan | create vlan guide]], [[Cisco Commands#rename vlan | rename vlan guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 100
Switch(config-vlan)#    name STUDENT
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

then give vlan 100 its svi (the gateway ip for that whole vlan) — [[Cisco Commands#enter vlan interface and setup vlan ip address | vlan interface + ip address guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface vlan 100
Switch(config-if)#      ip address 192.168.2.1 255.255.255.0
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## create vlan 200 after
same pair of commands as vlan 100 — [[Cisco Commands#create and configure vlan | create vlan guide]], [[Cisco Commands#rename vlan | rename vlan guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 200
Switch(config-vlan)#    name FACULTY
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

then the svi for vlan 200 — [[Cisco Commands#enter vlan interface and setup vlan ip address | vlan interface + ip address guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface vlan 200
Switch(config-if)#      ip address 192.168.3.1 255.255.255.0
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

> [!tip] after the vlan 200 svi you'll see the link up messages like this
> `%LINK-5-CHANGED: Interface Vlan200, changed state to up`

## trunk on the main switch (3560)
enter the gigabit port that points at the 2960, then trunk it — [[Cisco Commands#enter ethernet port interface | enter interface guide]], [[Cisco Commands#configure switchport to be mode trunk | trunk guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
> [!warning] the `encapsulation dot1q` line is only needed/possible on the 3560
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface gigabitEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

after this the main switch switching side is done — it should show Vlan100 and Vlan200 up in `show ip interface brief`

# sub switch (2960)
## enter the sub switch
it's a different device, so you have to enable + configure terminal on it again:
```cisco
Switch>                 enable
Switch#                 configure terminal
Switch(config)#
```

> [!note] check the pc ports first
> hover the cable ends or run `show ip interface brief` to see which fast ethernet ports pc0/pc1 are actually plugged into — we use Fa0/1 and Fa0/2 below

## trunk on the sub switch
the 2960 only supports 802.1Q so there is **no** `switchport trunk encapsulation` command here — just mode trunk. [[Cisco Commands#configure trunk on the second switch | second switch trunk guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface gigabitEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## create the 2 vlans on the sub switch
the sub switch needs its own copy of the vlans (vtp may sync them over the trunk, but making them by hand is safer) — [[Cisco Commands#create the vlans on the second switch | second switch vlan guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         vlan 100
Switch(config-vlan)#    name STUDENT
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         vlan 200
Switch(config-vlan)#    name FACULTY
Switch(config-vlan)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## access ports — 2 things to assign
### pc0's port → vlan 100
enter the fast ethernet port pc0 is on, make it an access port and put it in vlan 100 — [[Cisco Commands#assign access ports to vlans | access port guide]], [[Cisco Commands#setup for exit | exit guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface fastEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#      switchport access vlan 100
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

### pc1's port → vlan 200
same access block, different port and vlan — [[Cisco Commands#assign access ports to vlans | access port guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         interface fastEthernet 0/2
Switch(config-if)#      switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#      switchport access vlan 200
Switch(config-if)#      no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#      exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

> [!warning] do NOT add svis on the sub switch — no `interface vlan 100` / `interface vlan 200` with ip addresses here
> the sub switch is layer 2 only — the 3560 is the **only** device allowed to own `192.168.2.1` / `192.168.3.1`. if both switches hold the same ip:
> - the dhcp server pings an address before leasing it and gets a reply from the sub switch → `%DHCPD-4-PING_CONFLICT: DHCP address conflict: server pinged 192.168.2.1`
> - pcs can't tell which switch answers when they look for the gateway → pings die
> 
> if it already happened, delete the svis on the sub switch (`no interface vlan` removes the ip interface — the vlans, ports and trunk keep working):
> ```cisco
> Switch(config)#         no interface vlan 100
> Switch(config)#         no interface vlan 200
> Switch(config)#         do wr
> ```

# DHCP pools (back on the main switch)
this is the part that makes it a dhcp lab — everything below happens on the **3560's** cli (config mode). click back to the main device first

## exclude the gateway addresses first
a pool leases the whole `/24` starting at `.1` unless told not to — and `.1` is the svi you just made. exclude it on both subnets
**prompt:** `Switch(config)#`
```cisco
Switch(config)#         ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.2.1
Switch(config)#         ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.3.1
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## create the vlan100 pool
**prompt:** `Switch(config)#`
```cisco
ip dhcp pool vlan100
```

the prompt changes to `Switch(dhcp-config)#` — a pool needs 3 things:
```cisco
Switch(dhcp-config)#    network 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0
Switch(dhcp-config)#    default-router 192.168.2.1
Switch(dhcp-config)#    dns-server 192.168.2.1
Switch(dhcp-config)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

> [!tip] what the 3 lines mean
> - `network` — the range being handed out: `192.168.2.0/24` (minus the excluded `.1`)
> - `default-router` — the gateway pushed to the pc = the vlan 100 svi
> - `dns-server` — here it matches the svi too

## create the vlan200 pool
same block, vlan 200 numbers (`default-router` = the vlan 200 svi):
```cisco
Switch(config)#         ip dhcp pool vlan200
Switch(dhcp-config)#    network 192.168.3.0 255.255.255.0
Switch(dhcp-config)#    default-router 192.168.3.1
Switch(dhcp-config)#    dns-server 192.168.3.1
Switch(dhcp-config)#    exit
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

## enable ip routing
same "optional but do it" step as the other labs — without it the pcs can never ping across vlans even with dhcp — [[Cisco Commands#enable ip routing (optional) | ip routing guide]]
```cisco
Switch(config)#         ip routing
Switch(config)#         do wr
```

> [!tip] switched on the pools late, or already saw a `%DHCPD-4-PING_CONFLICT`?
> the server remembers old conflicted addresses. clear the lease table and let the pcs re-request — [[Cisco Commands#verify | verify guide]]
> ```cisco
> Switch#                 clear ip dhcp binding *
> ```

# the pcs
## get the ips via dhcp — 2 devices
click the pc → **desktop** tab → **ip configuration** → select **DHCP** (instead of typing a static set) — [[Cisco Commands#setup pc ip addresses | pc ip setup guide]]

no ip, mask, gateway or dns to type — the pool fills them all in (the pc shows "DHCP request successful"):
| pc | vlan | what it gets |
|----|------|--------------|
| pc0 | 100 STUDENT | `192.168.2.x` / `255.255.255.0` / gateway `192.168.2.1` |
| pc1 | 200 FACULTY | `192.168.3.x` / `255.255.255.0` / gateway `192.168.3.1` |

> [!tip] how to renew a lease
> the exact leased address depends on order, so check it: desktop → **command prompt** → `ipconfig`. if a pc is holding stale settings from an earlier attempt, toggle the radio to static then back to dhcp — that forces a fresh request. don't panic if pc0 keeps `192.168.2.2` and pc1 keeps `192.168.3.2` every time, dhcp reuses the next free address

on the switches, make sure you're at `Switch#` (privileged exec, not config mode) and run the standard trio on **both** — [[Cisco Commands#verify | verify guide]]
```cisco
Switch#                 show vlan brief
Switch#                 show interfaces trunk
Switch#                 show ip interface brief
```

on the 3560 you can also watch the leases:
```cisco
Switch#                 show ip dhcp binding
```

then from a pc (desktop → command prompt):
```bash
ipconfig
```
shows the leased ip/mask/gateway — pc0 should be `192.168.2.x` with gateway `192.168.2.1`

```bash
ping 192.168.3.2
```

first ping may drop 1-2 packets (arp) — run it again, it should pass. ping `192.168.3.1` too if you want to hit the gateway directly
